input.transcript:
User: What did Northern Alliance leaders agree on defence spending, and who objected?

Assistant: Northern Alliance leaders agreed to a joint defence spending goal of 5 percent of national output by 2035, which is divided into 3.5 percent for core defence and 1.5 percent for related spending such as resilience and cyber defence [Northern Alliance leaders adopt 5% spending goal](https://news.example/2026/06/alliance-summit-spending-target). However, Norland's prime minister objected to this target, calling it unrealistic for her country's economy and stating that it would lead to cuts in pensions rather than military spending. She mentioned that Norland's current spending level of 2.1 percent is sufficient and claimed that an exemption for members facing budget constraints was informally agreed upon, although this was not reflected in the official communiqué [Norland says 5% target is unrealistic](https://news.example/2026/06/norland-rejects-spending-target).

In contrast, Vestria supported the 5 percent target but disputed Norland's claim of an exemption, emphasizing that the communiqué is the complete agreement without any opt-out clause. Vestria's delegation also sought a broader definition of related spending to include infrastructure that supports defence readiness [Vestria backs target, asks for flexibility](https://news.example/2026/06/vestria-backs-target-with-caveats).

outline: Split of target: 3.5% core defence and 1.5% related spending
Norland's objections, current spending (2.1%) and exemption claim
Vestria's support, dispute of exemption claim, and push to broaden 'related' spending
Official communiqué versus alleged informal exemption

# Northern Alliance defence spending — transcript-based analysis

## 1. Joint 5% defence spending target (by 2035)
The transcript states that Northern Alliance leaders agreed to a joint defence spending goal of 5 percent of national output by 2035. This overall target is reported in the same source that summarized the summit agreement [Northern Alliance leaders adopt 5% spending goal](https://news.example/2026/06/alliance-summit-spending-target). The transcript does not provide the full text of the agreement or list which member states explicitly accepted the target beyond the general statement.

## 2. Split of target: 3.5% core defence and 1.5% related spending
According to the transcript, the 5 percent target is divided into 3.5 percent for core defence and 1.5 percent for "related spending" such as resilience and cyber defence. That division and the examples of related spending are reported in the same source as the overall target [Northern Alliance leaders adopt 5% spending goal](https://news.example/2026/06/alliance-summit-spending-target). The transcript does not elaborate on definitions, accounting rules, or verification mechanisms for distinguishing "core" from "related" spending.

## 3. Norland's objections, current spending (2.1%) and exemption claim
The transcript records that Norland's prime minister objected to the 5 percent target, calling it unrealistic for her country's economy and arguing it would force cuts in pensions rather than military spending. She stated that Norland's current defence spending level is 2.1 percent and characterized that level as sufficient. The prime minister also claimed that an exemption for members facing budget constraints had been informally agreed, but that claim was said to be absent from the official communiqué [Norland says 5% target is unrealistic](https://news.example/2026/06/norland-rejects-spending-target). The transcript does not provide Norland's full economic reasoning, budgetary analysis, or the text (if any) of the alleged informal exemption.

## 4. Vestria's support, dispute of exemption claim, and push to broaden 'related' spending
The transcript indicates that Vestria supported the 5 percent target and disputed Norland's claim that an exemption had been agreed. Vestria emphasized that the official communiqué represents the complete agreement and contains no opt-out clause. Separately, Vestria's delegation sought a broader definition of "related" spending to encompass infrastructure that supports defence readiness [Vestria backs target, asks for flexibility](https://news.example/2026/06/vestria-backs-target-with-caveats). The transcript does not include Vestria's proposed text for expanding "related" spending nor any reaction from other members to that proposal.

## 5. Official communiqué versus alleged informal exemption
The transcript presents a direct disagreement between Norland and Vestria over whether any exemption was agreed informally. Norland's prime minister claimed an informal exemption for members with budget constraints, but that exemption is not reflected in the official communiqué, per the same source reporting her statement [Norland says 5% target is unrealistic](https://news.example/2026/06/norland-rejects-spending-target). Vestria countered by stressing that the communiqué is the complete agreement and contains no opt-out clause [Vestria backs target, asks for flexibility](https://news.example/2026/06/vestria-backs-target-with-caveats). The transcript does not provide the text of the communiqué, any ancillary minutes, or corroboration from other delegations, so the existence and content of any informal exemption cannot be confirmed from the provided material.
